correctness.rationale: In a Heisenberg Lie algebra, adjacency depends only on the nondegenerate symplectic form on the central quotient. An independent set projects to pairwise orthogonal vectors, whose span is totally isotropic and therefore has dimension at most n. Counting all central lifts gives the sharp bound q(q^n-1), with equality exactly for maximal isotropic subspaces. The vertex-count/independence bound gives chi at least q^n+1, and an explicit Desarguesian symplectic spread of F_{q^n}^2 gives equality. Equality in the coloring bound forces every color class to be maximum independent, yielding exactly a symplectic spread. The packaged checker verifies the extremal counts and spread partitions for q=2,3 at n=2.

value.rationale: Chromatic and independence numbers are basic structural invariants for the graph introduced by the motivating paper. For the canonical Heisenberg family, the theorem determines both exactly and identifies every extremizer, converting graph coloring into the classical geometry of symplectic spreads. The result is reusable as an exact finite-field test family and strengthens a later general abelian-cover theorem by solving and classifying the cover problem in a natural nilpotent Lie family.
